# ForgeSworn

> ForgeSworn is an open-source workshop: apps you can use today and libraries you can build with, on Nostr, Lightning and plain cryptography, so that identity, money, files, location and conversations answer to the person rather than to a platform. MIT-licensed projects in eleven focus areas that work standalone or compose into full workflows. The live catalogue lists the current projects.

## Pages

- [Landing page](https://forgesworn.dev/): products you can run today, the creed, and the full repo catalogue grouped into eleven focus areas
- [Ecosystem map](https://forgesworn.dev/map/ecosystem-map.svg): every project on one page, grouped by what it does (SVG; printable A4 PDF at https://forgesworn.dev/map/ecosystem-map-a4.pdf)
- [Use cases](https://forgesworn.dev/use-cases.html): 32 end-to-end workflows, each naming the exact libraries it composes
- [4K listening room and comparison player](https://forgesworn.dev/media-lab.html): the complete licensed Deja Vu mix leads the homepage. Play & join starts or joins a shared listening clock and real RelaySwarm participation. For a new room, the first full-recording viewer prepares a bounded verified media reservoir locally before publishing the shared start time; preparation does not count as an active listener. A viewer still preparing a private start adopts a verified active room promptly, retires its empty old loader before the acknowledgement and preserves the original Play request; a failed acknowledgement restores an explicit retry. Cancelled or replaced asynchronous setup failures cannot fail a newer Play request; genuine current publication failures still restore retry. Existing rooms keep their advancing clocks and later listeners join live, the starter can leave while others continue, and the room expires after the last listener leaves a short grace period. Pause leaves; Play rejoins live. The recording loops while occupied; the 1080p excerpt has its own room. The live listener ticker includes joined listeners and excludes read-only page observers; Play/Pause events update it directly, with lease expiry for abrupt departures and unknown status during lost room observation. A confirmed empty room invites the first listener to start. One visible player per visitor, room participants distinct from locally connected peers, stable identity mapping through peerConnectionDetails(), proportional media-batch movement and rates, source-host feeds, explicitly self-reported remote links, separate loaded-source/verified-peer/upload counters and recent local peer contribution. Loaded source includes browser cache; playback details distinguish completed source response bodies from network and cache when timing coverage is available. Cache hits do not animate as fresh local network traffic; concealed timings remain unavailable. The browser integration pins RelaySwarm source 995383b6a3149177bd92e855deac06ec13b5d284 (package version 0.4.4). Connection setup waits for a first local ICE candidate if SDP is still empty at its 1.2-second soft cap, within the existing dial deadline; completion without a candidate refuses the dial. This corrects a captured empty-answer publication and does not establish sustained peer contribution or physical-phone playback for this pin. The integration retains bounded rolling startup planning, sustainable peer waits and range-sized WASM uploads. Startup preserves its verified contiguous future prefix before using the existing fourth residency slot even after the original first interval expires; that contiguous successor is not skipped by the previous fragment’s service-time lead once the target reaches both verified futures; the original first response is unchanged. The full-recording startup explicitly reserves a 32 MiB encoded aggregate including that response within the existing 64 MiB shared held budget; future bytes alone retain a 24 MiB cap, and non-startup playback keeps the SDK default. These are encoded reservoir limits, not total browser memory. Newly verified short peer pieces can refresh an older rate through a batch within one transfer and connection, retaining the 300 ms and 32 KiB floors, elapsed gaps and verification time. Origin bytes, duplicates and rejected responses cannot train this input; no first-byte timing sample or Rust/WASM binary change is introduced. The 27 October 330-second public pair on source 25354e3 and site acd26cd recorded 9 and 11 post-frame stalls, with fewer than 60 seconds observed after the wrap. That earlier sustained-playback check remains failed. A separate 28 October public-asset check on source 94bc0d2/site b88ab1e recorded zero observed post-frame stalls, player errors and dropped frames for two fresh headless Chrome viewers on one M4, including 74.041 seconds after the wrap; its dated evidence and same-host limits are linked below. Startup now has twelve seconds from the original first-fragment load entry, clipped to a shorter parent load deadline; ordinary speculative requests keep their eight-second expiry. Startup accepts parsed fragment start/duration roundoff within bounded machine precision, capped at one nanosecond, instead of falsely cancelling a matching context; sequence, continuity, level, key, size and duration checks remain authoritative. This does not establish stall-free or sustained 4K playback. A longer bounded wait does not establish successful real-source startup or alter required verified recovery headroom. Controlled correctness regressions do not establish reliable cold multi-viewer startup, decoded playback or traffic savings for this pin. When an owned source response finishes and its key is already known, eligible retained HAVE is published before FETCH withdrawal, including synchronous hls.js disposal; unknown keys do not delay playback for another hash. Cache/verification limits remain unchanged and no new peer-wait policy is enabled. This correction does not establish traffic savings or smoother playback. Peers exchange object-framing support in existing authenticated SDP offers and answers; an explicit version 2 is accepted only after current admitted SDP installation. Eligible new channels can therefore use verified range transfers before a periodic presence announcement; missing or unsupported values preserve conservative presence-derived behaviour. Admission, verification, upload limits and HTTP deadlines remain unchanged. Confirmed recorded main media requires a live same-key fetch lease before waiting for unavailable video; live and unknown playlists retain bounded seeding coordination. Sharing continues throughout active playback without an elapsed-time or cumulative-byte cutoff; upload rate, peers and cache remain bounded. Known pinned recordings use a client-generated bounded sliding live playlist with discontinuities across programme wraps and one visible player. The 267.32-second 4K programme preserves every original audio packet; a separately named, hash-pinned final fragment removes only 32 video frames after the soundtrack ends. The init and first 133 fragments remain byte-identical; the old immutable assets remain available. The next head can load before the tail ends; normal wraps do not end the element, reset its raw time or trigger replay priming. The bounded playlist retains 24 seconds of metadata behind the room clock so a slow initial response does not immediately eject the playhead; this does not enlarge the four-second media back buffer or encoded-media cache. A fixed per-session timeline origin maps raw media time to the shared clock; programme phase drives displayed time, telemetry and the musical pulse. Metadata preparation and peer creation remain after Play. Canonical manifest hashes and exact media URLs are checked, virtual global sequence/discontinuity values are signed against the unchanged piece catalogue, and a separate source/quality/epoch/manifest/duration cohort isolates this mode. Unsupported metadata and native HLS keep the ordinary VOD fallback; automatic clock corrections wait for sustained drift and stable, safely buffered playback, with the measured seek interruption added to the drift threshold, without changing music tempo. The responsive swarm picture keeps short labels and puts transfer rates and contribution statistics below it. A 16 KB score derived from the soundtrack drives a musical broadcast pulse against actual media time; pause, buffering, hidden pages and reduced motion stop it. This does not establish exact global audience counts or multi-speaker audio synchronisation. iPhone and iPad use the same peer-capable HLS path as other MediaSource-capable browsers; browser identity does not bypass sharing. The public Spry credential endpoint remains unconfigured pending an independently operated public endpoint. When configured, active playback requests and renews unique temporary TLS credentials from that independently operated instance, alongside STUN discovery. The supported public service uses its four-field credential contract and fresh one-hour leases, separately from KithMoot paired/private access. The final public instance endpoint remains operator configuration. This supplies a route for browsers that restrict direct UDP, including default Vanadium configurations. The bundle contains no relay password or operator root secret; availability diagnostics contain no credential. Pause cancels renewal. Issuer or route failure preserves HTTPS playback. Playback details can save or share a local JSON report with at most 240 one-second observations of actual frames, buffering, stalls and verified peer traffic, omitting network addresses, keys and credentials; no report is uploaded automatically. The HLS module prepares before Play without media requests or a player. The first tap attaches the selected media source and requests audible playback before awaiting room or peer setup; initial playback no longer waits for paused priming. This preserves request ordering but does not establish physical iPhone acceptance or stall-free startup. VOD fallback replay can still use a safely buffered current position while retaining buffered correction to the room. Reports retain raw media position/buffers and expose recording phase/duration separately; infinite continuous-media duration stays unavailable rather than being relabelled as the finite recording duration. Healthy network-stalled events with future data do not count as playback waits. The deployed 26 October 330-second same-M4 run used two fresh HTTP-cache-disabled Chrome profiles and the actual CDN assets, with no asset, controller or RTC overrides. Both had zero observed post-frame stalls/drops through the programme wrap and at least 60 seconds afterwards; accepted peer shares were 21.05% and 45.31%. First frames took 12.979 and 5.030 seconds. One midway report export per viewer remained in all measurements; A retained one nonfatal pre-frame aborted fragment event with no post-frame error increase. This is sampled same-host evidence, not physical-phone, independent-network, public TURN, wire-cost or eight-person-call acceptance. The earlier lab route passed public browser credential/CORS and hash-verified TLS data checks; that test route was retired. Fresh public-instance issuance, actual lease rotation during playback, independent-network cold-cache 4K and physical iPhone acceptance on the current revision remain separate gates. Positive peer waits require actual origin timing; a cold loader starts HTTP immediately while cached and late-HAVE peers retain their parallel race. Positive waits are bounded by the segment duration after measured origin recovery time; cached peer races start HTTP immediately and use an explicit peer-only Rust ranged planner with no internal HTTP source. The demo enables lateHaveRace: only native connections accepted at load entry can participate, after an actual exact-object HAVE arrives within the original 2.5-second window. HTTP continues immediately; one holder set is frozen and the deadline never extends. A verified calibration piece unlocks bounded pending work. Four-piece and 512 KiB request caps retain upload burst bounds for larger fragments. At the floor the peer arm cancels while its independent HTTP request continues. Normal buffered mixed transfers retain their HTTP ranges; older modules safely decline the unsupported mode. Range uploads copy the requested bytes across the WASM boundary, rather than the whole 4K object for every range. A separately packaged module Worker reuses the compiled Rust/WASM module for bounded piece scheduling and payload verification; HTTP continues during Worker startup or failure, and leaving the swarm terminates it. The bundle receipt pins the companion source and digest. This separates verification work from playback controls; measured device continuity and useful peer contribution remain acceptance checks. On native-HLS-capable browsers, repeated stalls can switch playback to native HLS; anonymous CORS is set before selecting the approved cross-origin media, peer resources close and native transfer totals are marked unavailable. Native recovery requests playback immediately and restores phase on metadata without a second Play; a later pause or policy rejection stays authoritative. Saved reports retain fixed HLS/native error codes, fallback reason and failed state without arbitrary messages or URLs. Terminal media failure restores Play again. A real Chrome recovery test decoded 333 native 4K frames with zero drops over 13 seconds after an intentional fatal Hls event; the transition interrupted playback for 3.827 seconds. This is recovery evidence, not sustained cold-cache or physical-phone acceptance. The Rust/WASM scheduler exchanges site-verified pieces of the unchanged 4K source, with HTTP completing the remainder, native controls, a Back to live action and shared-room invitation links. Integrity uses a site-pinned HTTPS digest catalogue with receiver-local commitment signing. Resource limits and reproduction: https://github.com/forgesworn/forgesworn.dev/blob/main/docs/media-showcase.md. The local runner compares native Sapflow and MediaMTX with the same H.264/AAC source and optionally real RelaySwarm delivery through Spry or coturn over UDP/TCP. Public process results are dated recordings; live origin CPU requires the local runner. Reproduction: https://github.com/forgesworn/forgesworn.dev/blob/main/docs/media-lab.md

Two fresh headless Chrome viewers recorded zero post-frame stalls, player errors and dropped frames, including 74.041 seconds after the programme wrap. First frames 4.328/1.799 seconds; accepted peer shares 13.431%/46.943%. Guarded preservation applied 10/13 times; neither this count nor the healthy run establishes causal improvement or traffic savings. Early rich report rows remain unknown. No phone, independent-network, public TURN, synchronisation or competitor qualification; earlier failures remain unchanged.
- [Deployed 4K playback evidence](https://github.com/forgesworn/forgesworn.dev/blob/main/docs/evidence/public-prepared-adoption-4k-20261026.json): dated 26 October 2026; two fresh Chrome profiles on one M4 Max, actual public assets, 330 seconds each, zero observed post-frame stalls/drops, 21.05% / 45.31% accepted peer media. Missing measurements remain null. Evaluation counts are not requests, verified pieces are not playback credit, and these receipts do not establish throughput or savings. No identifiers, raw SDK records, new requests, timers or selection policy are added. The partialUsefulnessPreserved counter records only a current transfer/link whose fresh verified-piece timestamp survives its owned positive-body HTTP winner; zero-credit attempts retain ordinary cooldown and no Hls credit or rate is invented. Older SDKs leave the new counter unknown. The XHR loader’s final binary progress callback claims HTTP immediately; one guarded microtask permits success with a nonempty binary body before queued retirement to use the existing ownership proof. Positive nonbinary progress retains immediate cancellation. Progress alone or success after retirement cannot preserve or restore usefulness. No playback-performance improvement is established.

## Products people can use today

- [flock](https://flock.forgesworn.dev): coercion-resistant group locator; end-to-end encrypted location over Nostr, guidance by voice, sound and vibration (source: https://github.com/forgesworn/flock)
- [KithMoot](https://kithmoot.forgesworn.dev): multi-device video rooms over Nostr; a room is a secret held by whoever has the link, and a person on two devices appears as one participant (source: https://github.com/forgesworn/kithmoot, Android: https://github.com/forgesworn/kithmoot-android)
- [DonkeyRide](https://donkeyride.forgesworn.dev/about): ride-hailing and dispatch with nobody in the middle taking a cut; reference implementation of the TROTT protocol (source: https://github.com/TheCryptoDonkey/donkeyride)
- [Wildbloom](https://wildbloom.forgesworn.dev): browser encryption, replicated or erasure-coded storage pools, owner-controlled repair, trusted signed node recommendations, optional direct-to-operator checkout and fresh full-read storage audits. Archipelago defaults uploads to the operator's own node and lets that operator opt in to sell a bounded share at their own prices and terms. ForgeSworn provides the software, not a storage service or marketplace (source: https://github.com/forgesworn/wildbloom)
- notecase and moneyer: an LNURLcash (LUD-25) bearer-note wallet and mint (npm: @forgesworn/notecase, @forgesworn/moneyer)
- [Heartwood](https://heartwood.forgesworn.dev): hardware Nostr signer on an ESP32 with a keyless bridge; clients bark (browser, https://bark.forgesworn.dev) and cambium (Android, https://cambium.forgesworn.dev)
- [Bray](https://bray.forgesworn.dev): trust-aware Nostr MCP server for AI agents (npm: nostr-bray)
- [My Signet](https://mysignet.app): decentralised identity verification with ZK age proofs; drop-in SDK signet-verify
- Kintrinsic: libre, self-hosted digital wardship on a family's own keys (source: https://github.com/forgesworn/kintrinsic, SDK on npm: @forgesworn/charter)

## Key libraries

- [toll-booth](https://github.com/forgesworn/toll-booth): L402 middleware, any HTTP API becomes Lightning-payable in one line (npm: @forgesworn/toll-booth). Try `npx @forgesworn/toll-booth demo` or the live demo at https://jokes.forgesworn.dev
- [402-mcp](https://github.com/forgesworn/402-mcp): MCP client so AI agents can discover, pay for, and consume L402/x402 APIs (npm: 402-mcp)
- [nwc-kit](https://github.com/forgesworn/nwc-kit): small, security-focused NIP-47 Nostr Wallet Connect client (npm: @forgesworn/nwc-kit); site at https://nwc-kit.forgesworn.dev
- [nwc-lnd-bridge](https://github.com/forgesworn/nwc-lnd-bridge): minimal NIP-47 wallet service in front of an LND node, invoice-only by default
- [farrier-kit](https://github.com/forgesworn/farrier-kit): Lightning payment primitives without running a node: BOLT-11 decoding, preimage verification, LNURL-pay resolution (npm: farrier-kit)
- [moneyer](https://github.com/forgesworn/moneyer) and [notecase](https://github.com/forgesworn/notecase): LNURLcash (LUD-25) mint and crash-safe wallet for Lightning bearer notes
- [bray](https://github.com/forgesworn/bray): trust-aware Nostr MCP server for AI agents, 258 tools across identity, social, payments, dispatch, trust, and privacy (npm: nostr-bray)
- [nsec-tree](https://github.com/forgesworn/nsec-tree): deterministic Nostr sub-identity derivation, one master secret, unlimited unlinkable identities (npm: nsec-tree)
- [heartwood](https://github.com/forgesworn/heartwood): keyless NIP-46 bridge for hardware Nostr signers (ESP32 or Ledger)
- [signet](https://github.com/forgesworn/signet): decentralised identity verification, tiers, Signet Score, ZKP age proofs (npm: signet-protocol); user app at https://mysignet.app
- [canary-kit](https://github.com/forgesworn/canary-kit): deepfake-proof spoken verification with silent duress detection (npm: canary-kit)
- [dominion](https://github.com/forgesworn/dominion): epoch-based encrypted access control with tiered audiences (npm: dominion-protocol)
- [kintrinsic](https://github.com/forgesworn/kintrinsic): self-hosted digital wardship; guardian app, Android ward app, Linux warden, Nostr wire contract (npm SDK: @forgesworn/charter)
- [wildbloom](https://github.com/forgesworn/wildbloom), [wildbloom-node](https://github.com/forgesworn/wildbloom-node), [shelter-kit](https://github.com/forgesworn/shelter-kit): encrypted, content-addressed Blossom storage over HTTPS or optional Tor: browser client, self-hosted node and Rust storage core. Pool recovery needs the signed receipt, recovery key and enough surviving parts. Full-read audits prove current retrievability, not continuous custody. ForgeSworn Link integration is planned, not a current Wildbloom transport.
- [kithmoot](https://github.com/forgesworn/kithmoot): multi-device conference rooms over Nostr; second implementation in Kotlin at kithmoot-android
- [Live media stack](https://forgesworn.dev/live-media.html): build live broadcasts with Sapflow SRT/RTMP ingest, LL-HLS packaging and optional recording; add RelaySwarm peer-assisted HLS and operator-selected Spry TURN when needed. Public MIT libraries. The film-led 4K listening room shows actual visitor connections and delivery; direct peers and HTTP fallback run in the public browser. Automatic Spry TLS access awaits the operator endpoint; native Spry/coturn comparisons remain local. Native adapters and physical-device acceptance have separate qualification gates.
- [Live media benchmarks](https://forgesworn.dev/live-media-benchmarks.html): methods, versions and raw results for Sapflow, RelaySwarm and Spry TURN. In the 23 October 2026 M4 Max loopback test with 750 simulated viewers, Sapflow's optional own HTTP loop with 16 workers used 79% less CPU and 90% less process RSS than MediaMTX 1.21.2; default Hyper used 64% less CPU. These are workload-specific measurements, not deployment capacity guarantees.
- [Spry TURN](https://forgesworn.dev/live-media.html#spry): optional MIT Rust STUN/TURN relay, separate from Sapflow ingest and HLS. Public 0.2.1 binaries delivered 16–22% more UDP and 27–35% more TLS packets/s than tested coturn 4.18.0 on M4 Max; TCP ranged from 1.2% behind to 8.5% ahead. Linux ARM64 VM results were mixed. The linked benchmark report retains all 108 M4 samples, platform limits and corrected RelaySwarm composition results: UDP passed; TCP/TLS timing gates remain open, and TLS lacked an active selected path at the final sample. Actual KithMoot web generated-media calls passed local UDP/TCP/TLS qualification with operator credentials; cross-network and physical-phone acceptance remain open. Source: https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn.
- [relayswarm](https://github.com/forgesworn/relayswarm): peer-assisted HLS live streaming with WebRTC signalling over Nostr relays instead of a tracker; Swift port relayswarm-kit
- [nostr-veil](https://github.com/forgesworn/nostr-veil): anonymous trust assertions via LSAG ring signatures over NIP-85 (npm: nostr-veil)
- [nostr-anon-vote](https://github.com/forgesworn/nostr-anon-vote): anonymous voting on Nostr with LSAG ring signatures (npm: nostr-anon-vote)
- [rendezvous-kit](https://github.com/forgesworn/rendezvous-kit): fair meeting points for N participants via isochrone intersection (npm: rendezvous-kit)
- [gopherkind](https://github.com/forgesworn/gopherkind): signed gopherholes served from Nostr relays (kind 31436), with Gopher, Gemini, HTTP and CLI readers (npm: gopherkind); site at https://gopherkind.com
- [ring-sig](https://github.com/forgesworn/ring-sig), [range-proof](https://github.com/forgesworn/range-proof), [shamir-words](https://github.com/forgesworn/shamir-words), [private-equality](https://github.com/forgesworn/private-equality): standalone cryptographic primitives (npm: @forgesworn/*)
- [anvil](https://github.com/forgesworn/anvil): supply-chain-hardened npm release tool, reproducible two-runner builds, OIDC trusted publishing, SLSA provenance
- [nip-drafts](https://github.com/forgesworn/nip-drafts): 30 draft Nostr protocol extensions
